newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish debt market lacked fuel on Friday afternoon as the U.S. dollar pulled down the peseta versus the mark, dealers said.
"But bonos proved to be stronger than others. Have a look at the spread versus Bunds...that briefly broke 90 basis points," a Madrid-based dealer said.
The 10-year cash spread versus Bunds narrowed briefly to below 90 bps and ended at 90, lower than 93 bps at the start.
Traders also took a note of optimism from the long bond future, which ended above the 115 level, now considered a new support. The long future hit a record high on Friday at 115.32.
The general tone of the bond market was seen as positive and a few dealers suggested that the long future could easily climb toward 116 if foreign markets would allow it.
"Especially if April CPI comes in as good as we are expecting the market will steam to new highs," a dealer said.
April CPI, due on May 14, is seen showing a year-on-year increase lower than 2.0 percent. Spain's inflation rate hit a 29-year low in March at 2.2 percent.
"Today on the market there were bullish people saying that the Bank of Spain could even cut 50 basis points on Friday of next week," a dealer in Madrid added.
